verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents a REST API with a toggle-feature endpoint, an official MCP server that makes authenticated REST calls, and a runtime probe that created a flag through the API. It also documents draft revisions that must be approved before publishing, and an API 'Require confirmation' setting that holds risky changes for human review. However, approval enforcement on agent or API writes rests on a single line, and approval workflows appear only on the top pricing tier, so complete coverage is not shown. Missing for 10: detailed documentation that approval rules gate API/MCP-originated flag changes to production, no documented CLI, independent or hands-on corroboration of the approval enforcement, and availability below the top pricing tier.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
The official GrowthBook MCP server is a thin bridge: it loads GrowthBook Agent Skills (workflows and guardrails) and makes authenticated calls to the GrowthBook REST API.
Draft feature revisions, request review, resolve merge conflicts, and require approval before publishing.
Require confirmation holds risky changes until a person confirms them in GrowthBook.
Pro, plus: Custom environments Ramp schedules Approval workflows
